Definition: from G3581; hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment:--lodging.
BiblicalUsage: Many came to Paul in his lodging in Rome, to hear him expound the kingdom, and Paul writes to Philemon, prepare me also a lodging, for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a lodging is never just a room in the New Testament: Paul's lodging became a pulpit, and Philemon's guest room was an act of faith that Paul would come home.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
